plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether a high-contrast dielectric pair (ZnS/MgF2) in an alternating stack can achieve dual-band transmission at 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm while suppressing 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm. The design draws from recalled thin-film optics principles: high index contrast enables broader stopbands, and non-quarter-wave thickness tuning can create multiple passbands within a single stack. This route was planned from the model's own prior knowledge alone with no retrieved literature. Repaired to use explicit substrate dataset name 'Daimon-20' to resolve registry ambiguity.

routes.title: ZnS-MgF2 Alternating Dual-Band IR Filter on Daimon-20 Substrate
routes.scientific_hypothesis: An alternating high-low index dielectric stack with individually tunable layer thicknesses can produce two distinct transmission bands in the 4 μm region while maintaining suppression in adjacent stopbands, without requiring complex non-periodic topologies.
routes.design_principle: Recalled thin-film optics: dielectric mirrors produce stopbands centered at quarter-wave optical thickness. By deviating from strict quarter-wave thicknesses and allowing each layer to vary independently, multiple transmission windows can emerge within the broader reflection band. ZnS (high index ~2.2-2.3 in mid-IR) and MgF2 (low index ~1.3-1.4 in mid-IR) provide sufficient index contrast for effective band shaping.
routes.proposed_topology: 22-layer alternating stack starting with ZnS: [ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2] on Daimon-20 substrate, air incident medium
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 22 layers, each tunable independently within 50-1000 nm bounds
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
maximize mean transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: ZnS and MgF2 are conventional IR-depositable dielectrics
thickness bounds 50-1000 nm are within typical deposition capability
theory_basis: Recalled: quarter-wave stacks produce high reflectance bands; deviating from quarter-wave can create transmission windows within stopbands
Recalled: index contrast between ZnS and MgF2 in mid-IR is sufficient for effective interference filtering
Recalled: alternating high-low stacks are manufacturable via physical vapor deposition or chemical vapor deposition
Recalled: CaF2 (Daimon-20 dataset) is transparent in the 3-5 μm region and serves as appropriate IR substrate
expected_advantages: High index contrast enables strong spectral shaping with fewer layers
Alternating topology is simple to manufacture and model
Individual thickness tuning allows optimization of dual-band response without topology changes
ZnS and MgF2 are both in the guaranteed material name list and should resolve correctly
known_risks: Exact refractive indices of ZnS and MgF2 at 4 μm wavelength are recalled approximately; actual measured data from registry will determine performance
22 layers may not provide sufficient degrees of freedom for both passbands and both stopbands simultaneously - may need to increase to 24 layers if optimization stalls
Thickness bounds (50-1000 nm) are estimated from recalled deposition limits; actual manufacturable ranges may differ
No literature was consulted to verify optimal material pairs for this specific wavelength region
Daimon-20 is used to resolve CaF2 substrate ambiguity; if this dataset name fails registry resolution, the route would need repair with Daimon-25 instead
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 22-layer planar multilayer infrared filter coating on CaF2 (Daimon-20) substrate with air incident medium at normal incidence. Use alternating ZnS and MgF2 layers starting with ZnS as layer 1. Optimize individual thicknesses for all 22 layers within bounds 50-1000 nm. Spectral range 3500-5300 nm. Maximize mean transmittance in passbands 4150-4350 nm and 4550-4750 nm. Minimize mean transmittance in stopbands 3600-4000 nm and 4850-5200 nm. Use coherent thin-film matrix method. No metal layers. Total layer count exactly 22.
routes.revision_reason: Iteration 16 failed due to material_data issues with ambiguous CaF2 substrate name. This revision replaces 'CaF2' with explicit dataset name 'Daimon-20' as instructed by registry diagnostic. Maintains the ZnS/MgF2 material pair from successful earlier iterations (04, 08, 12) while fixing the substrate resolution defect. Material names are copied exactly to ensure registry resolution.

valid_candidates count should remain above zero if material data resolves correctly
tightest_margin should not fall systematically across rounds if the optimization remains in feasible region
thicknesses_nm should show non-uniform distribution if the optimizer finds non-quarter-wave solutions that improve dual-band response

if valid_candidates falls to zero for two consecutive rounds, relax thickness bounds by 20% and continue
if tightest_margin falls below 0.1 for three consecutive rounds, reduce optimizer step-size by 50% and continue

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
